nodes.label: Dependabot config (.github/dependabot.yml)
nodes.rationale: commit-message prefixes (ci / chore) are set so Dependabot's default 'Bump X from A to B' subject is rewritten into a Conventional Commit — otherwise it would be invisible to version-calculation tooling that parses commit subjects. Minor/patch updates are grouped into one PR per ecosystem while majors fall outside the group, so a major bump is read on its own rather than buried in a batch.

nodes.label: github-actions ecosystem updates (repo root)
nodes.rationale: Keeps SHA-pinned actions current: Dependabot rewrites the pinned SHA and its trailing version comment together, so pinning does not mean going unpatched.

nodes.label: npm ecosystem updates (/spotmap-website directory)
nodes.rationale: Directory is /spotmap-website because the Angular app is nested — package.json does not live at the repository root.

nodes.label: CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
nodes.rationale: Triggers on pull_request into main or dev; contents: read only since no job writes anything; a per-ref concurrency group cancels an in-flight run when the PR gets a new push.

nodes.label: test job — unit tests (Karma, headless Chrome)
nodes.norm_label: test job — unit tests (karma, headless chrome)

nodes.label: secrets job — gitleaks secret scan
nodes.rationale: Installs the MIT-licensed gitleaks binary directly (not gitleaks-action, which is license-gated for organization accounts), pinned by version + SHA256 together, checksum-verified, because Dependabot cannot see a version pinned inside a run: block.

nodes.label: npm run build:pages
nodes.rationale: Chains the tools/ test suite, the production build, and both deploy-artifact verifiers, so this one step gates the artifact main deploys.

nodes.label: Deploy Angular App to GitHub Pages workflow (.github/workflows/deploy-angular.yml)
nodes.rationale: Triggers on push to main. Least privilege: top-level contents: read; the build job stays read-only (contents: read, pages: read) and only the deploy job elevates (pages: write, id-token: write) for itself, running only after build succeeds (needs: build).

nodes.label: The Phosphor Archive (creative north star)
nodes.rationale: Every surface should read as a green-phosphor CRT terminal from before the web looked modern; glow is the light source, not decoration. Discipline to two phosphors (green as default voice, amber as the rare care/selection channel) is deliberate: amber only means 'pay attention' if it stays rare. Explicitly rejects corporate/Google-Maps neutrality, Strava/Instagram social polish, cutesy gamification, and 'modern dark-mode SaaS' — dark alone is not the same as this; retro-computing intent is the difference.

nodes.label: The Two-Phosphor Rule
nodes.rationale: Only green and amber are voices; green is default, amber is earnest/selected; everything else is a near-black tint of green. Any third decorative color is forbidden.

nodes.label: The No-White Rule
nodes.rationale: #ffffff and near-white grays are banned on every surface, the basemap included. White is the failure signature — empty/loading/error states fall back to `surface`, and white-arriving map chrome (MapLibre popup box, tip, attribution) is repainted. Ruled 2026-09-13 that phosphor-bright (#b6ffb6) is exempt: it's a pale mint at full saturation, not near-white, confirmed by an on-device sweep finding no pixel with all three channels above 200.

nodes.label: The Rarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Amber covers <=10% of any screen; if a screen has amber in more than one role at once, cut back to the single most-earnest one, preserving amber's meaning as 'attention.'

nodes.label: The One-Grid Rule
nodes.rationale: Everything is monospace; no proportional font enters the interface, not even for 'friendly' body copy or headings — the grid is the brand.

nodes.label: The Restrained-Caps Rule
nodes.rationale: UPPERCASE + tracking is reserved for labels and terminal system-copy only, never body prose, because long uppercase runs kill the sunlight read.

nodes.label: The Glow-Is-The-Shadow Rule
nodes.rationale: Never add a dark/gray box-shadow or filter: drop-shadow(black). Elevation is always a colored phosphor bloom (green, or amber for the care channel) — raise glow, not a gray shadow.

nodes.label: The Bloom-Budget Rule
nodes.rationale: Glow must not smear legibility: resting text glow stays <=6px radius so letters keep clean edges in sunlight; only non-text chrome (frames, active tabs) uses the wide 24-30px halos.

nodes.label: Directions link (Google Maps dir URL)
nodes.rationale: Kept as a Google Maps web directions URL, opened in a new tab, because it is the only single URL that reaches a native maps app on both phone platforms and still degrades to a usable route everywhere else; a geo: URI has no iOS handler and maps.apple.com deep-links only on Apple platforms. Opening in a new context leaves the archive tab (map, selected pin, open popup) standing rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: tools/verify-css-asset-urls.mjs
nodes.rationale: Fonts live under src/fonts/ (not public/) so the bundler emits them hashed and rewrites the url() relative; a root-absolute /fonts/... path would 404 under the deploy prefix, and this script guards against that regression.
